Miniaudio
Miniaudio is a single file audio playback and capture library for C and C++. It supports a wide range of platforms and audio backends, making it a versatile choice for audio applications. Miniaudio is designed to be easy to use, with a simple API that abstracts away the complexities of audio programming.
Miniaudio supports various audio formats, including WAV, MP3, OGG, and FLAC. It also provides features such as audio mixing, resampling, and effects processing. The library is lightweight and efficient, making it suitable for real-time audio applications.
Miniaudio is open-source and can be found on GitHub. It is licensed under the MIT License, allowing for flexible use in both commercial and non-commercial projects. The library is actively maintained and has a growing community of users and contributors.

Version: 0.11.25
License: MIT License

libvorbis
libvorbis is a free and open-source audio compression library that implements the Ogg Vorbis audio format. It is designed to provide high-quality audio compression while maintaining a small file size. libvorbis is widely used for encoding and decoding audio in various applications, including music streaming, gaming, and multimedia software.
libvorbis is developed by the Xiph.Org Foundation and is licensed under the BSD license. It supports a wide range of platforms and is available for use in both C and C++ applications. The library provides a simple API for encoding and decoding audio, making it easy to integrate into existing projects.

libogg
libogg is a free and open-source library for handling the Ogg multimedia container format. It
provides a simple API for reading and writing Ogg files, as well as for handling Ogg streams. libogg is widely used in conjunction with other libraries, such as libvorbis, to create and manipulate Ogg Vorbis audio files.
libogg is developed by the Xiph.Org Foundation and is licensed under the BSD license. It supports a wide range of platforms and is available for use in both C and C++ applications. The library is designed to be efficient and easy to use, making it a popular choice for multimedia applications.
